rule: Objective-C relationship truth and completeness audit
method: every file the router admits across 3 pinned repos (NO sampling). Three independent questions, each answered from a different arbiter. PHANTOM/UNRESOLVED: every edge's target is looked up in the analyzer's own symbols for that file, then in a source-side set of names the file actually declares or defines, then against a system-name pattern — so an edge is called unresolved only when nothing in the file, the symbol table or a system namespace accounts for it. SILENT: source-side construct counts (message sends, selector keywords, allocations, protocol declarations and conformances, superclass refs, properties, synthesised ivars, methods, C functions, imports) are counted from comment- and string-stripped text and compared against what the analyzer bound. FAMILY: the two managed-OO conformance types are read off a real file to see whether a consumer can separate them.
why: a symbol count and a clean ERROR count say nothing about whether an edge is TRUE or whether a construct is MISSING. The lane had 8 corpus-backed relationship types and 24,114 edges and no measurement of either.

targetResolution.note: selectorOrModulePath counts three shapes that cannot be resolved by a name lookup and must not be counted as failures: SELECTOR targets (`alloc`), QUALIFIED SUPERCLASS MEMBERS (`UITableViewCell.initWithStyle:reuseIdentifier:` — absent from the subclass file by definition, which is what an override IS), and PATH targets (`Foundation/Foundation.h`, `SDWebImageCompat.h` — a `w+` token can never match a name containing a dot).

A FABRICATED target is a name the emitting file never contains — not a symbol, not a token, not a path. That is a real phantom: a consumer routing on the edge has nothing to aim at. The first version of this audit instead asked whether the target was DECLARED in the file, omitted block parameters from the declaration set, and reported 55.6% of all edges as unresolved when the top case (`uses -> image`) was a block parameter read one line after its declaration. Scoped honestly: this catches fabrication, and does NOT judge whether an edge means what a reader would want.

completeness.note: source-side construct counts vs analyzer output. A construct with a large source count and ~0 bound edges is a SILENT construct; the ratio is the signal and it is deliberately not turned into a verdict, because the two sides count different things (a message send inside an ERROR region is in the source count and cannot be in the edge set).

verdict: payload complete: 24,114 edges, all with a line and an evidenceClass. 8 relationship families, every one corpus-backed. 0 distinct FABRICATED target name(s) (0% of edges) — names the emitting file does not contain.
